name: P-022 Round-Leader Dead-Heat Fade Maker (retrospective spec v2, corrected close resolution)

close_resolution.rule: close_epoch comes ONLY from the external ESPN-derived schedule. Resolve (product_metadata.competition, series-derived round, product_metadata.competition_scope) -> round-end UTC. There is NO Kalshi-field fallback.
close_resolution.kalshi_time_fields_are_unusable: close_time, occurrence_datetime, expiration_time, expected_expiration_time and latest_expiration_time ALL collapse to one conservative far-future placeholder while the market is OPEN; close_time is rewritten to the true value only at the instant the market closes. This is exchange-wide, not a golf quirk, and it is NOT reversed for this family. src/round_leader_fade_maker.py contains zero references to any of these fields.
close_resolution.fails_closed: resolve_event_close returns None -> DO NOT QUOTE. Three paths produce None and all of them mean no quote: (a) event has no product_metadata.competition, (b) the resolver raises, (c) the resolver has no round-end for that (competition, round). Unresolved events are recorded in pod.unresolved_events with a reason. A wrong round time is worse than no quote.
close_resolution.calibrated_to_err_early: src/golf_schedule.py is deliberately calibrated to predict the round end EARLY — validated one-sided on 72 of 72 settled events, minimum +0.16h. Predicting a close LATE would put resting orders into a live round.
close_resolution.must_be_re_resolved: Books are RE-RESOLVED, not timed once at discovery. ESPN publishes no tee times ~3 days out, so the coarse per-tour day offset is what is available at listing time and the answer sharpens as the event approaches.
close_resolution.history: The pod ran 2026-07-23 to 2026-07-26 writing ZERO quotes because it anchored on occurrence_datetime. The first fix swapped the field priority to close_time; that was ALSO wrong (still a placeholder on an open market) and was superseded on 2026-07-27/28 by this external schedule. strat_p022_fade_v1 failed integrity for describing that superseded field-priority rule as current.

anchor_price_band.reference: mid_price of the YES orderbook at time of evaluation
anchor_price_band.rule: eligible_to_quote iff 0.03 <= mid_price <= 0.12; recompute every cycle, do not cache

posting_window.measured_from: the EXTERNALLY resolved close_epoch above, never a Kalshi field
posting_window.rule: can_place_new_quote iff 12.0 <= hours_to_close(close_epoch) <= 24.0; once placed a quote RESTS UNCHANGED to close — no re-quoting or re-pricing inside 12h
posting_window.outside_window_behavior: outside [12h,24h] the engine discovers markets and settles positions but places NO new quotes

excluded_from_entry: quotes placed inside 12h to close are non-compliant with the locked posting-window cap and must be EXCLUDED from T (P022_DECISION_RULE.md §7)
events whose close could not be externally resolved — no quote is placed at all, so they contribute nothing

exit_logic.rule: No discretionary exit. A resting maker quote is either filled and held to settlement, or pulled unfilled via cap exhaustion or the kill switch.
quote_pull_triggers: data/KILL_ROUND_LEADER_FADE present -> pull ALL resting quotes immediately
per-name, per-tournament or aggregate collateral cap exhausted -> pull the quote that would breach it
mid_price leaves [0.03,0.12] before fill on an unfilled resting quote -> re-evaluate/pull next cycle

settlement_mapping.result_no: settlement_value = 0.00 — note a WITHDRAWAL on this family settles NO, not a fair-value scalar; that is the top-N/GOLFFINISH template, a different rulebook
settlement_mapping.result_scalar: settlement_value = settlement_value_dollars from the per-ticker GET. PARTIAL PAYOUT, NEVER a void. Booked WIN/LOSS on the sign of (fill.price - payout - fee). If settlement_value_dollars is absent the pod logs and DEFERS to the next cycle rather than defaulting to zero.
settlement_mapping.result_void: excluded from P&L entirely — applies only to a market that never resolved, never to result=scalar

fair_value_model.description: Fair value is not a probability estimate. It is the certified contract term that a tie for the round lead splits the $1.00 notional $1/n (rounded down) across tied names. Verified verbatim from PGAROUNDLEADER.pdf: the clause carries NO conditional carve-out, unlike LEAGUELEADER.pdf which governs the KXLEADER* family and makes its split contingent on the league not declaring a winner through official tiebreakers.
fair_value_model.mechanism_class: settlement-mechanic hypothesis, not a probability-disagreement hypothesis. No CLV substitute is valid for this family — round-leader markets have no sharp external closing line (P022_DECISION_RULE.md §8.5).

fee_model.computation: src.kalshi_fees.fee_per_contract(price, series_ticker=<ticker>) — series_ticker MUST be passed; lookup is EXACT match against src/fixtures/kalshi_series_fees.json, never prefix logic
fee_model.assertion: all 13 series are `quadratic` (maker-free). Verified in the v1 integrity review against both the generated fixture and a live GET /series/KXPGAR1LEAD. scripts/p022_checkpoint.py --check-fees asserts this live rather than assuming it.
fee_model.taker_fee_not_applicable: P-022 is maker-only; the taker formula 0.07*P*(1-P) does not apply to its own fills

risk_limits.sizing_basis: collateral_at_risk = (1 - quote_px) per contract, NEVER contract count
risk_limits.cap_enforcement_rule: each new quote is sized to the tightest remaining of {per-name, per-tournament, aggregate}; the quote is pulled the instant any cap is exhausted
risk_limits.cap_scope_caveat: P-022 runs as its own process, so AggregateRiskGuard reservations bind against P-022's OWN book only — the 15% aggregate cap is NOT enforced against the 5-minute engine's other positions
risk_limits.cap_is_gate_condition: these caps are GATE CONDITIONS, not tuning knobs (P022_DECISION_RULE.md §7/§8.1). A tournament with ANY cap breached is EXCLUDED from T. Raising ANY cap resets T to 0 and requires re-registration under a new pod ID (P-022b). This spec does not loosen any value above.

null_hypothesis: Net of the maker fee (zero for this family) and net of adverse selection in real resting fills, the equal-weighted-across-tournament, contract-weighted-within-tournament mean settlement P&L per filled contract — for selling YES in [0.03,0.12] at mid+0.02, posted 12-24h before an EXTERNALLY resolved round close on KX*R{1,2,3}LEAD — is not reliably positive. Retrospectively: the backtest point estimate is <= 0, or its tournament-clustered 95% CI includes 0.
alternative_hypothesis: The unconditional $1/n dead-heat split, combined with retail longshot overpricing on cheap round-leader names, produces a positive net edge per filled contract that survives fees (zero here), the modelled fill process, and tournament-level clustering — i.e. a tournament-clustered 95% CI strictly above 0 on the retrospective sample.

extra.validation_target: The RETROSPECTIVE Phase-2 backtest ONLY, recomputed from golf_quirks_research/ harness + data. NOT the live forward gate.
extra.boundary_not_to_cross: P-022's live forward gate is at T>=24 (Amendment 1, 2026-07-28). T is currently 0 and P022_DECISION_RULE.md forbids an early look. No artifact in this chain may compute, estimate or report a live forward-gate statistic. scripts/p022_checkpoint.py is the only sanctioned reader and is not invoked here.
extra.decision_rule_locked_reference: golf_quirks_research/P022_DECISION_RULE.md, LOCKED 2026-07-26, Amendment 1 2026-07-28 (T=14 -> T=24). Reproduced without loosening: HARD KILL z<=-2.0 at any T; NO DECISION T<24; at T>=24 KILL if edge<=0, PASS if z>=2.0, else ONE extension to T=40 at byte-identical parameters then KILL if still z<2.0.
extra.unit_of_observation: ONE TOURNAMENT = one observation. R1/R2/R3 events of the same tournament pool to a single observation, not three. Within-tournament statistic is the contract-weighted mean net per-contract P&L; the across-tournament aggregate is the equal-weighted mean of those per-tournament statistics. Bootstrap CIs cluster by tournament.
